transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um... I hope I’m in the right place, and I really don't want to sound like I'm just being difficult or complaining. 

I’m here because for months now, I’ve been seeing this... well, this pattern. My sister’s appointments keep getting moved around, our bills keep showing up wrong, and people just seem to constantly "forget" to call me back. Everyone keeps telling me it’s just innocent mistakes or administrative oversights, and I always try to be understanding, I really do. But... well, I know they’re keeping information from me. It really feels like they're trying to push me out of important decisions. 

I'm sorry if that sounds a bit much, I just... I know what I'm seeing. Does that make sense why I'd want to come in and talk to someone about it?
Are you experiencing any other unusual sensory perceptions, such as hearing voices or seeing things that others around you do not seem to notice?

Oh, no, no. Nothing like that at all. I, um... I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. I know me coming in and talking about people hiding things might make it sound like I'm... well, you know. But my mind is perfectly clear, I promise. 

Everything I'm noticing is right there in the paperwork and the schedules, just... real, everyday things. I haven't had any sort of visions or voices. I hope that's a good sign? I really just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information and not making myself sound, um, worse than I am. Am I explaining that okay?
Do you feel this way only about the specific people involved in these administrative issues, or do you find yourself feeling suspicious or mistreated by most people you encounter in your daily life?

Oh, um, no, it's really just the people involved with my sister's care and the billing office. I'm actually a very trusting person normally! I supervise an administrative team myself, so I work with people all day long, and I get along with everyone just fine. I don't go around thinking the cashier at the grocery store or my neighbors are out to get me, I promise. 

It's really only this specific situation because... well, because I'm seeing the actual paperwork and the schedules changing. I hope that makes sense? I really don't want you to think I'm just a suspicious or paranoid person in general, because I'm really not. I just... I care about my sister, and I want to make sure things are handled right. Is it okay that I'm just concerned about this one area?
Have you ever tried to confront these individuals with the specific documents or evidence you've found, and if so, how did they respond?

Well, I... I have brought it up, yes. I try to be very polite about it, of course! I don't want to be one of those difficult family members who yells at the staff. I know how hard they work. 

So, I've taken the schedules in, and the billing statements, and I just... I point out the discrepancies very gently. But they always just smile and say it was a computer glitch, or that someone put the wrong code in, or that a shift changed at the last minute. They're very nice about it, usually, but they never actually fix the root of the problem, and the mistakes keep happening. 

I don't push it too hard because I don't want them to think I'm accusing them of anything terrible, even though... well, even though I know they're doing it on purpose to keep me out of the loop. I just nod and thank them for their time. I hope that's the right way to handle it? I really don't want to cause a scene or make anyone uncomfortable.

Has this situation with the paperwork and the feeling of being kept out of the loop caused you any significant distress or interfered with your ability to perform your own job or manage your other daily responsibilities?

Oh, um, no, not really. I mean, it is stressful, of course, because I care so much about her. But I wouldn't say it's interfering with my life in a bad way. 

I still go to work every day, and my team is doing great. I keep my house very tidy, I pay all my own bills right on time... I'm still managing everything just fine. I know some of my friends or... well, maybe even the staff at the facility... might think I'm a little too focused on all this paperwork. But I'm certainly not falling apart or acting strangely or anything like that. Outside of just trying to get straight answers for my sister, everything else is completely normal. 

I really try to keep it balanced, you know? I don't want this to take over my whole life, and I think I'm doing a pretty good job of keeping it contained. Does that sound like I'm handling it okay? I just want to make sure I'm dealing with this the right way.

When your friends or the staff at the facility suggest that you are being too focused on this paperwork, do you ever feel that they are part of a coordinated effort to gaslight you or cover up their mistakes?

Oh, um... well, "coordinated effort" sounds so... aggressive, doesn't it? I really don't want to sound like one of those people who thinks everyone is out to get them. I'm not like that at all, I promise. 

But... well, yes, I suppose I do feel like they're working together sometimes. Not in a malicious way! Just... I’m here because for months now I’ve been seeing the exact same pattern. It's not just a one-time thing. My sister’s appointments get moved without anyone telling me, the bills show up with the wrong codes, and people just... "forget" to call me back. 

And even when my friends or the staff tell me it’s just honest mistakes, or that I'm looking too closely at it... I just know they’re keeping information from me. It feels like they're trying to push me out of making decisions for her. I try to be so polite about it, but it's hard when you can clearly see what's happening, you know? 

I hope it doesn't sound terrible that I think that. I just want to protect my sister. Is it okay that I feel that way when the pattern is so obvious?
